feature: A clip's sound is on the timeline from the moment it opens
summary: Every clip with sound now shows it as its own segment with a waveform on an Audio track under the picture, linked the way Premiere links a clip's audio: drag either one and both move. Drag the line to set the volume, drag a top corner handle to fade, and right-click, Detach Audio to unlink them.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open a screen recording that has sound, then press V for Select. The sound sits on an Audio track under V1.
Drag the green sound segment to the right. The picture above comes with it.
Press Cmd-Z, then drag the pale line on the sound segment down a little. The whole line drops and the clip plays quieter.
Drag the small square at the segment's top left corner to the right. The line now rises out of silence: a fade in.
Right-click the sound segment and choose Detach Audio.
Drag the sound segment again. Now only the sound moves; the picture stays put.
Drop a second recording and some music onto the timeline. Each clip, and both halves of one an insert split, has its own sound under it; the music gets Audio 2.

evaluate: Does a Premiere editor find the clip's audio where they expect it, on A1 under V1?
Is it clear enough that the picture and its sound are one thing until you detach them, from the shared highlight alone?
Is the line easy to catch for a volume drag without grabbing the clip by mistake?
Are the fade handles findable when they only show on a picked or hovered segment?
When music is dropped straight onto the Audio track, is it right that the recording's own sound steps down to a new track, rather than being overwritten as Premiere would?
rough: A sound's waveform appears about a second after it lands, while the file is read; until then its segment is a plain green bar.
A linked segment moves only along time. Carrying it up or down to another audio track is not built.
Dropping music onto the track holding a recording's sound moves the recording's sound down a track instead of overwriting it the way Premiere would.
Deleting the Audio track under a clip takes that clip's sound away and keeps its picture, as deleting A1 does in Premiere.
The mock's small 'duck -8 dB' tag on the audio clip is not drawn; the level shows as the line only.
The right-click menu on a clip holds Detach Audio, Split at Playhead and Delete only. The full clip menu is the open task on right-click everywhere on the timeline.
The Detach Audio button in the panel is still there alongside the right-click.
